clue.text: Despite being injured, mother got on

parts.note: a dam is a mother, especially of an animal
to have got on is to have grown old, to have aged

explanation.surface: Someone presses ahead even though hurt, mother continuing regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damaged has been harmed, just as an injured thing has been hurt.

clue.text: Buy preserve, and find oneself in trouble

explanation.surface: Purchasing a jar of jam leads to a predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase means to obtain some jam; idiomatically it means to land in difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, acquiring a jar of fruit preserve; idiomatically, ending up stuck in a difficult situation.

clue.text: Hit by workers' action

explanation.surface: A business is struck by industrial action from its staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow landed is a strike, and a walkout by employees is also called a strike.

clue.text: How to read a palindrome

parts.note: a palindrome reads the same in either direction, so you can read it forwards and then back again

explanation.surface: A simple question about reading words like 'level' or 'radar'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving back and forth describes reading in both directions, which a palindrome allows.

clue.text: Rough lad fretted direly in Fagin's employ

indicators.note: direly suggests something done terribly or badly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A tough boy worries terribly while working for a Dickensian villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'direly' rearranges ROUGH LAD FRETTED. The definition 'in Fagin's employ' points to the young pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist, and the fodder 'Rough lad' also describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Dawkins, nicknamed so in Oliver Twist, is the pickpocket working for the criminal Fagin.

clue.text: Such a road wrecked a trailer

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, so the letters of these words are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A trailer has been wrecked on a main road.
explanation.definitionFit: An arterial road is a major through-route, like the main artery of a body.

clue.text: Lawman wants cleaner for country-house

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American law officer

indicators.note: wants here means lacks, so the word for the cleaner is short of its final letter

parts.note: a char is a cleaning woman, short for charwoman

explanation.surface: A lawyer is looking for a cleaner to look after a house in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants' means 'lacks': CHAR drops its last letter R to give CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian second home or villa in the countryside.

clue.text: Decline to give a briefing

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to provide a summary of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling-off in condition is a run-down; a summary report is also a run-down.

clue.text: Obvious way to get copyright

explanation.surface: A plain method for securing rights to your work.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent means plainly evident; it is also legal protection granting exclusive rights to an invention.

clue.text: Topping hospital department initially full of charm

indicators.note: initially says the hospital department piece comes first, at the start

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department in a hospital
icing is the sugary topping on a cake

explanation.surface: A top-notch hospital unit seems charming from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' tempts as an adjective meaning excellent, but here it is the noun for a cake covering; 'initially' places the hospital department first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enticing is alluring and attractive, full of appeal.

clue.text: Put herb in charge of a church

parts.note: basil is a culinary herb
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a herb responsible for a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large church with special privileges, such as St Peter's in Rome.

clue.text: Reckon it's of concern to a lad

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning, as in a letter heading
a son is a boy, a lad

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a matter is worrying for a young boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to think things through logically, to calculate or work out.

clue.text: Emergency keeps labour on the qui vive

parts.note: red is the colour associated with the Labour Party and the left
on the qui vive is a French-derived phrase meaning watchful, on guard

explanation.surface: In a crisis, the workforce stays watchful.
explanation.walkthrough: Red is the colour of Britain's Labour Party; 'keeps' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase denotes the highest state of readiness for danger, a crisis situation.

clue.text: Nationalistic bombast is outrageous!

parts.note: flag-waving is nationalistic display, so flag stands for it
a rant is a loud, bombastic tirade

explanation.surface: Patriotic ranting is condemned as shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means glaring and shocking, conspicuously offensive.

clue.text: Mean to bring HM back here

indicators.note: bring back means the letters for the Queen are reversed

parts.note: Her Majesty, the Queen, is ER (Elizabeth Regina)
being here is being present

explanation.surface: An intention to return Her Majesty to this place.
explanation.walkthrough: HM is Her Majesty; ER (Elizabeth Regina) brought 'back' becomes RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something is to stand for or signify it.

clue.text: Entire triangle is out of true

indicators.note: out of true means misaligned or distorted, so the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A whole triangle has been drawn crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral can mean whole and complete, with nothing lacking.

clue.text: Last semester in Alabama

parts.note: a semester is an academic term
AL is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Alabama

explanation.surface: A student's final half-year spent in a Southern state.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminal means final, coming at the end.

clue.text: Said I was headhunted? Rubbish!

indicators.note: said signals that the words are spoken, so they are matched to a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the first letter of hunted, its head, follows I WAS to give the run IWASH

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have been poached by recruiters, and the listener scoffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headhunted' gives the H from the head of 'hunted' placed after I WAS; 'Said' means the result, I WASH, is heard as the word for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is nonsense or humbug, talk meant to deceive.

clue.text: Struggles to compose melodies

explanation.surface: Someone finds it hard to write tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Strains are great efforts; strains are also passages of music or tunes.

clue.text: Individual is utterly tactful

indicators.note: utterly read as 'when uttered' means the word is spoken and matched to one sounding alike

parts.note: a tactful person is discreet

explanation.surface: A person is said to be entirely diplomatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' looks like 'completely' but means 'in speech'; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means separate and distinct, each unit standing alone.

clue.text: Haven in Seychelles ideal for athletes

indicators.note: in places the harbour inside the country code

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle code for the Seychelles
a port is a harbour or haven

explanation.surface: An island harbour that suits sportspeople.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sporty is fond of and good at athletic games.

clue.text: Soldiers' signal recovery

parts.note: RE are the Royal Engineers, soldiers, and the S comes from the possessive
a cue is a signal to act

explanation.surface: A soldiers' signal that someone has been retrieved.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescue is the saving or retrieval of someone from danger.

clue.text: Many panegyrics contain symbolic messages

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
odes are poems of praise, panegyrics

explanation.surface: Numerous poems of praise hide secret meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Codes are systems of symbols used to convey hidden information.

clue.text: Upset, sad and moody before final judgment

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is gloomy and down ahead of a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like a mood alongside sad and moody but rearranges SAD and MOODY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Last Judgment in Christian belief is said to come on the day the world ends.

clue.text: No easy option for committed users

definitions.text: No easy option for committed users

parts.words: No easy option for committed users
parts.note: the clue reads as a tough choice for devotees, but 'No easy' is hard and committed users are addicts

explanation.surface: A tough alternative for dedicated customers.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroin and cocaine are narcotics that addicts are hooked on, the opposite of soft ones.

clue.text: His landlord keeps pole in a tepee

indicators.note: in puts the pole and the letter inside the tepee

parts.note: a tepee is a type of tent
N is the North pole

explanation.surface: A landlord holds a pole inside a tepee.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is whom 'his landlord keeps': a renter housed by a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupant who rents property from a landlord, who lets out the property to him.

clue.text: Artist's referee, maybe

explanation.surface: A painter is perhaps an umpire.
explanation.walkthrough: James McNeill Whistler was an American painter; a referee blows a whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistler was a famous painter; a referee or anyone blowing a whistle is also one.
